correctness.rationale: The 14-vertex Heawood incidence graph (points P_i, lines L_j with P_{j,j+1,j+3}) has exactly 3^14=4,782,969 labelled states. Deterministic rule 1->2,2->0,0->1 iff adjacent excited yields one successor per state. The original package includes census_indegree.cpp and paths-based alternative. Independently implemented a new C++ 4,782,969-state enumeration: construct all successor indices, peel indegree-zero vertices, traverse precisely surviving cycles for true least periods, then reverse peel order for exact preperiod T and eventual period P. Obtained 55 positive (T,P) classes, 21,099 periodic states, primitive orbit counts {1:1,3:5334,4:224,5:84,6:42,8:168,10:84,14:96}, entry populations T0..10 (21099,305203,1303711,1272154,1100708,526918,168336,42840,17136,12768,12096), no T>10 and all T10 in P4. Exhaustiveness follows from explicit iteration over every integer 0..3^14-1 and correct functional-graph peeling; the calculation is a finite proof, not extrapolation. lcm of periods is 840 so F^850=F^10 and 840 minimal.

originality.rationale: Best of knowledge: Doba 2018 and Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff 2018 establish qualitative synchrony/periodic-state and excitation-rate results for general graph Greenberg–Hastings dynamics. Their primary mathematical theorems and searchable full texts do not enumerate the Heawood 55-class entry-time/period table, its eight primitive orbit counts, or sharp ten-update entry bound. Resultary exact-dynamics records concern other specific graphs; no earlier Heawood numerical census identified. A preexisting unindexed exact computation remains possible.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the unique smallest cubic girth-six cage and a canonical finite incidence graph. A complete labelled-state 4.8-million-state functional-graph census yields the exact rare-period spectrum, basin-entry distribution and sharp global transient; these are nontrivial natural benchmark invariants for excitable network dynamics. Finite size does not diminish value because the entire natural model is classified, with exhaustive reproducible evidence.
